14454a4a8fa4c279.title: Maxiramin A Tablet
14454a4a8fa4c279.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supplementation of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, C and zinc during physical fatigue, pregnancy/lactation, reduced stamina during or after illness, growth periods, and old age, and for relief of eye dryness, night blindness (difficulty seeing in the dark), and prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets.
14454a4a8fa4c279.usage:
Children aged 12 and older and adults: take 1 tablet once daily.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
14454a4a8fa4c279.caution:
Warning: Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant should not take this medicine. Overdose in children aged 6 or under may cause fatal iron poisoning, so store out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; infants under 12 months; hyperkalemia; Wilson's disease; hemochromatosis (iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism); hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; kidney stones; severe renal failure; or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you have hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in urine); are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; cardiac/circulatory dysfunction; renal impairment; hypoproteinemia; gallbladder-related disease; liver disease; gallbladder obstruction; copper deficiency; alkalosis; diabetes; gout, kidney stones, or a history of kidney stones; or are hypersensitive or allergic to Yellow No. 5. If there is no improvement after about a month of use, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

This medicine may turn urine yellow, affecting clinical test values, and may interfere with the detection of blood glucose in urine tests.

Do not take with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracyclines, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist when taking with cardiac glycosides, estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, gastric discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, hives, photosensitivity, abdominal/stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, upper abdominal pain, red spots, cardiac arrest, central nervous system depression, hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, gas/bloating, gastrointestinal pain, dermatitis, body odor in sweat/breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, pulmonary edema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, increasing in amount, or bleeding for a prolonged period occur, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins A, D, E, B-group, C and zinc for fatigue, pregnancy/lactation, recovery, growth and old age
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, reduced stamina, eye dryness, night blindness, poor bone/tooth development, rickets

2d55aded7a3f6d36.title: Lopezicon Chewable Tablet
2d55aded7a3f6d36.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to control abdominal bloating due to intestinal gas and diarrhea accompanied by cramping.
2d55aded7a3f6d36.usage:
Ages 12 and older and adults: take an initial dose of 2 tablets chewed with water; if loose stools continue, take 1 tablet chewed with water. Do not exceed 4 tablets per day.
Children aged 9–11: initial dose of 1 tablet chewed with water; if loose stools continue, 1/2 tablet chewed with water. Do not exceed 3 tablets per day.
Children aged 6–8: initial dose of 1 tablet chewed with water; if loose stools continue, 1/2 tablet chewed with water. Do not exceed 2 tablets per day.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
2d55aded7a3f6d36.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: high fever of 38°C or above; bloody or mucoid stools; or a history of rash or allergic reaction to loperamide hydrochloride.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you would take it for 2 or more days; have a history of liver disease; are pregnant or breastfeeding; or have a history of abnormal heart rhythm.

Consult a pharmacist when taking with antibiotics.

If acute pancreatitis or similar occurs, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Controls diarrhea with cramping and gas-related abdominal bloating
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Diarrhea with cramping, abdominal bloating from intestinal gas
